security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU claims Smehv/Ssehv extension support (e.g., via misa or ISA string) but does not implement the EHV WARL bit in the xivt CSR (mivt=0x307, sivt=0x107) field layout, or implements the EHV bit as writable but ignores it during synchronous exception delivery — continuing to use the standard mtvec/stvec direct/vectored dispatch instead of the hardware-vectored entry point at xtvec + offset
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: riscv_cpu_do_interrupt reads env->mtvec/env->stvec directly without checking a corresponding xivt.EHV WARL field to determine whether synchronous exceptions should be hardware-vectored; CSR write functions for mivt/sivt accept EHV bit writes but the value is never consulted in cpu_helper.c trap delivery
security_spec.summary: Smehv/Ssehv repurposes xivt CSR low bits to hold a WARL EHV gate; if QEMU adds mivt/sivt without wiring EHV into exception dispatch, guest software relying on hardware-vectored synchronous exceptions traps to the wrong PC, breaking privilege boundary transitions

findings.finding: Trap delivery to S-mode uses env->stvec with standard direct/vectored dispatch ((stvec >> 2 << 2) + offset). No EHV hardware-vectored logic exists because QEMU does not claim Smehv/Ssehv support. There is no xivt CSR nor EHV WARL bit to check, so this is correct behavior for the current feature set.

Trap delivery to M-mode uses env->mtvec with standard direct/vectored dispatch. No xivt.EHV check is needed because no mivt/sivt CSRs exist in this codebase and no Smehv/Ssehv ISA extension is declared.

CSR mtvec write correctly validates mode bits [1:0] (0=direct, 1=vectored, >=2 reserved). No EHV-related mivt CSR (0x307) read/write functions exist. The CSR array has no mivt or sivt entries, consistent with not advertising Smehv/Ssehv.
Reset handler does not initialize mivt/sivt CSR state because these CSRs do not exist. No stale or wrong reset values can leak because the extension is entirely absent.
Migration vmstate has no mivt/sivt fields (only hvien/hvictl for AIA). Since no Smehv/Ssehv CSRs exist, there is no risk of silent corruption on live migration from missing fields.
KVM CSR reset and synchronization path only handles stvec (not mivt/sivt). No KVM sync gap exists because Smehv/Ssehv is not implemented on either the QEMU or KVM side.
